CITIES REQUIRING SPECIAL CONSIDERATION AND OTHER RELATED ISSUES:

New York, N.Y.
The Interim Report contains a brief synopsis of the historical evolution of existing rules and regulations concerning the commercial zone of New York City, Commercial Zones, 124 M.C.C. at 175-78. As we noted in that discussion, the New York-New Jersey area has been the subject of numerous proceedings, and a puzzling patchwork of regulations has Although it is unnecessary to repeat the entire emerged. Interim Report discussion devoted to New York City, a few succinct comments describing the existing situation are appropriate. It has previously been determined that the New York, N.Y., commercial zone extends 5 miles beyond its corporate limits in conformity with the original population-mileage formula, Commercial Zones, 53 M.C.C. at 496. Nevertheless, the exemption provided by section 203(b)(8) has been, for the most part, withheld with respect to the New York City commercial zone. For reasons relating to the National Transportation Policy, former Division 5 removed the exemption with respect to transportation between points in the New York, N.Y., commercial zone, except with respect to (a) transportation performed wholly within the New York, N.Y., commercial zone as defined in 1 M.C.C. 665, or (b) transportation which is performed with respect to a shipment which has had a prior or subsequent movement by either water carrier or rail carrier and is performed wholly between points in the New York, N.Y., zone as defined in 1 M.C.C. 665,
